criteria.scenario_coverage: Cover helper behavior through the scenarios of linked callers with traceable links.
criteria.setup_region: Allow a small checked preamble in assertions for fallible fixture construction.

criteria.error_rows: Explore an explicit bounded error parameter kind for reusable operation contracts.
criteria.fixed_bounds: Keep helpers specialized per error set with fully spelled concrete contracts.
criteria.result_data: Prefer data-level outcome types plus boundary adapters, deferring contract generics.

failure_abstraction.instructions: For helpers reused across unrelated failure domains, which line of work comes first?

criteria.author_callback: Support author-supplied reporters behind a boundary that tolerates reporter failure.
criteria.builtin_auto: Emit one sanitized diagnostic per request failure automatically with correlation identity.
criteria.manual_only: Leave all boundary reporting to handwritten per-handler recovery and logging.

criteria.catalogue: Keep extending compiler-owned operations deliberately as concrete products demand them.
criteria.companion: Publish the closed scope and steer the remainder to companion runtimes or services.
criteria.reviewed_adapters: Admit vetted adapter packages under a conformance regime covering errors, ownership, and packaging.

criteria.bounded_policy: Recommend bounded shapes only and revisit when a concrete workload forces the issue.

criteria.self_tail: Recognize self-tail relay patterns and emit equivalent native loops for them.

criteria.deployment_limits: Answer latency operationally through tuned infrastructure and honest documentation.
criteria.operation_deadlines: Ground every native wait in an effective deadline, then combine budgets per request.
criteria.scope_policy: Supervise unfinished branches explicitly so answers need not await abandoned work.

criteria.interop_ui: Hand rendering to outside frameworks and keep Can at the contract edge.

criteria.syntax: Invest in new UI syntax only alongside a demonstrated library shortfall.

state.assertions: Functions must ship named examples, but rows accept expressions only, so a throwing foreign constructor has nowhere to be handled inline and direct owner fabrication stays correctly forbidden. Consumer packages may hide the construction in a private total helper that raises a standard fault when the constructor unexpectedly rejects, yet each such shim adds declarations, rows, and reader burden. No setup grammar survived the LD29 scope ruling.
state.failure_observation: The serve edge maps every surprise to the same bare 500 and records nothing on its own. Handlers can match standard failures and write level-and-message lines, with SQLSTATE-style codes assisting database diagnosis, but uniform coverage needs every author to repeat the pattern. Main entry, cleanup ownership, and browser dispatch each report exactly once per occurrence in redacted form; the HTTP request path alone lacks that backstop.
state.host_boundary: Host power arrives only through the reviewed catalogue: packages cannot self-register bindings, scripts, or SDK bridges. Snapshots expose four event facts, namespaced attribute setting cannot steer live controls, and several browser subsystems have no Can projection at all. Outbound HTTP honors literal origins with tight path rules. Because managed processes and service calls already cover server-side escape, the sharp edge is absent browser-local capability.
state.iteration: Emitted async-thunk recursion keeps frames on the native stack prior to the first suspension, so a tail countdown passes one hundred rounds and dies approaching twenty thousand on the pinned runtime. Folds over realized arrays already escape this trap through chained continuations. Genuinely open-ended drivers such as pagers and machines need their own tested story that keeps argument semantics, completion identity, fixture linkage, and step diagnostics; limits stay environmental, never portable constants.
state.library_errors: Checked generic calls now cross package lines for values, but their failure bounds stay rigid: emits entries must be nominal declarations, and variables there are refused. Catalogue combinators enjoy precise per-callback bounds denied to authors. Teams either clone helpers per domain or ferry failures as ordinary variant data with hand-rolled adaptation. The missing piece is shared infrastructure that keeps two alien error sets distinct while serving both callers.
state.lifetime: Winners resolve and losers linger: ownership drains every branch before roots close, so HTTP responses wait out abandoned racers and the probe record confirms roots pending post-selection. Database awaits carry no caller clock, lock-wait tuning does not cap execution, and Can offers no timeout-setting statement. Server-side requests race real deadlines whereas browser action calls cannot even name one. Shutdown closes sessions then depends on supervisors past the waiting deadline, with ambiguous commits reported as unknown rather than guessed.
state.objective: Decide whether Can earns a broader SaaS recommendation and what would secure it. There is no installed base and no legacy syntax to protect. Immutable data, declared failures, and leased ownership are fixed points. Emitted code should be idiomatic native operations, never reimplementation behind helpers, except where contract adapters are unavoidable. Advice here informs design only and changes no sources.
state.progress: The tree at 2cb1bc3 already mounts shared actions with per-request actors, audits browser output into paired content-addressed assets, proves generic callees symbolically, and reconciles uncertain commits at the application layer. Keep those wins fenced: new work extends them, and any proposal that silently weakens them is out of bounds.
state.ui: Working Can code already drives keyed rows, field drafts, revision checks, announcements, and safe teardown, paying verbosity on every control and rebuilding views wholesale. Records plus named functions plus callables remain an untried but plausible factoring route. Live DOM truth must precede reuse claims, and fresh syntax waits for a library attempt to expose a real gap.
